gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on a Club Car Precedent the stock charger works through the cart's On-Board Computer (OBC), which is built to charge lead-acid batteries, so a lithium swap means bypassing the OBC and using a 58.4 V lithium charger, which the Vatrer and Redodo 48 V kits include.
standout_why: I opened the cited clubcar.com/en-us/personal/golf-carts page. It mentions lithium only as a powertrain option with 'no upkeep' and regenerative braking. It says nothing about chargers, the OBC, the BMS, voltage or converting a lead-acid cart. The cited T&T 4-passenger inventory page showed no listings and never uses the word lithium. The uncited clubcar.com/en/lithium-ion page says factory lithium is 'Available on new Tempo vehicles' and says nothing about retrofitting. ChatGPT asked the shopper whether they want a new cart or a battery upgrade, but none of its results explains what makes an upgrade work on an existing cart.
decides: If the shopper is upgrading a Club Car Precedent or a later DS, a 48 V battery alone won't work. The PowerDrive/OBC charging path has to be bypassed and replaced with a lithium charger. That favours complete kits that ship with a matched 58.4 V charger: the Vatrer 48V 105Ah Club Car kit at $1,579.99 or the Redodo 48V 100Ah kit at $1,149.99. It rules out a battery-only purchase that relies on the old charger. If the shopper is buying a new cart, the factory lithium Onward or Tempo avoids the problem, since Club Car integrates the pack, a 375 A controller and a CAN-bus Vehicle Control Module.

findings.product: general (Club Car PowerDrive Plus / OBC carts)
findings.label: OBC sits in the charging circuit
findings.value: "The negative terminal of the receptacle is connected to the onboard computer"; the OBC "will retain in memory the amount of charge needed to fully replenish the batteries"
findings.source_title: Club Car 1998 Maintenance and Service Manual Supplement, p. 14-3 (ManualsLib mirror)
findings.note: Club Car's own service manual, read on a third-party mirror. It describes the PowerDrive / PowerDrive Plus charge circuit and also warns "DO NOT BYPASS THE SENSE LEAD FUSE!". It says nothing about battery chemistry.

findings.label: OBC bypass required for a lithium conversion
findings.value: "the OBC must be bypassed using a jumper harness, because the OBC's charging profile is incompatible with lithium chemistry"; bypass "mandatory on most 48V Club Car models"
findings.source_title: ROYPOW, Club Car Lithium Conversion Guide: Everything You Need Before You Buy
findings.note: Published 2026-06-24 with no author credited. ROYPOW sells lithium conversion kits. It ties the OBC to the Precedent (2004 to present) and later DS models.

findings.note: The same page names a Vehicle Control Module on CAN bus, an IP67 steel battery case and a 1,000 W dynamic brake resistor. It says the pack is 'Available on new Tempo vehicles' and lists no voltage or kWh.
